texts.preamble: Narasappa vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 19 January, 2026 Kabc020015292022 Before The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore. (Scch-9) Dated This The 19th Day Of January 2026 Present: Smt.Nirmala.M.C,B.Com.,L.L.B Judge & Acjm, Court Of Small Causes. Mvc No.269/2022 Petitioner: Sri. Narasappa, S/o. Late Venkataswamy, Aged about 75 years, R/at Belachikkana Colony, Thondebhavi, Gouribidnur, Chikkaballapura, Karnataka - 561213. (By Sri. Kenchappa - Adv.) V/s. Respondents: 1. Iffco Tokio General Insurance Co., Ltd., Shanthi Towers, 5th Floor, 3rd main, 141, East of Ngef Layout, Kasturi Nagara, Bangalore - 560 043. (policy No.M1128653 valid from 30.01.2021 to 29.01.2022) (By Sri. N.Mahesh Prasad - Adv.) 2. Sri Ragavendra, S/o. Shriramashetty, Chikkamaluru, Kodigenahalli Hobli, Madhugiri Taluk, Tumkur, Karnataka - 572 132. (By Sri. R.Sunil Kumar - Adv. ) Scch - 09 2 Mvc No.269/2022 :: J U D G M E N T :
texts.facts: : The petitioner has filed this claim petition against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest for the Narasappa vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 19 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58341115/ 1 injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic Accident. 2. The brief contents of the petition are as under: On 23.10.2021 at about 10.00 pm., when the petitioner was travelling in a bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B- 9051 from Vokkaligara Samudhaya Bhavana S.S.Ghati Tobagere Hobli, Doddaballapura Taluk near Happy Valley resorts, the driver of the bus drove the same with a very high speed, recklessness and suddenly dashed to the road safety guard at right side bus fell down. Due to said impact, the petitioner and other passengers were forcibly knocked down and were sustained multiple grievous injuries. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital Doddaballapura wherein he took treatment as an inpatient for more than 6 days and spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards his SCCH - 09 3 MVC No.269/2022 treatment and nourishment. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was doing forming work and earning Rs.25,000/- per month. The accident in question occurred due to the rash and negligent manner of driving of Bus bearing reg.No.KA-06- B-9051 by its driver and the jurisdictional Doddaballapura Rural police have registered a case in their crime No.287/2021, after investigation the said police have filed a charge sheet against the said driver, punishable under Section 279, 338 & 304(A) of IPC. The first respondent being the insurer and the second respondent being the owner of said Bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B-9051 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, on all these grounds, the petitioner prayed to allow this petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- under all heads together with interest and costs. 3. In response to the Court notice, the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through their SCCH - 09 4 MVC No.269/2022 counsel and respondent No.1 and 2 have filed their respective written statement. 4. The brief contentions of the written statement of respondent No.1 are as under: The respondent contended that, petition is not maintainable in law, facts and circumstances of the case and petition is liable to be dismissed against this respondent. Respondent denied the place, date and time of alleged accident and also denied the income and avocation of the petitioner. Respondent contended that, compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant. Further denied the involvement of Bus bearing No.KA-06- B-9051 in the alleged accident. Further contended that, driver of the Bus was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident. Further contended that, the said Bus bearing reg.No.KA-060B-9051 was not having valid permit and FC as on the date of accident. Further the respondent No.1 has contended that, the owner of the vehicle and the concerned police have not SCCH - 09 5 MVC No.269/2022 complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act. Respondent admitted the issuance of Narasappa vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 19 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58341115/ 2 policy of insurance in favour of second respondent in respect of Bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B-9051 the liability of this respondent company if any is limited to the terms and conditions of the policy. Hence, on all these contentions, the respondent No.1 prayed to dismiss the petition against it. Hence, on all these contentions, the respondent No.2 prayed to dismiss the petition against it. 5. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :
texts.arguments: The brief contentions of the written statement of respondent No.2 are as under: The respondent contended that, petition is not maintainable in law, facts and circumstances of the case and petition is liable to be dismissed against this respondent. Respondent denied the place, date and time of alleged accident and also denied the income and avocation of the petitioner. Respondent contended that, compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant. Further contended that, alleged bus possess valid policy and driver of the said bus also holds valid and effective SCCH - 09 6 MVC No.269/2022 driving licence. The petitioner has contended that, on account of the said injuries, he has severe pain, suffering from deep mental shock and agony, very dull due to the accident, cannot sit, squat, stand, walk, climbing stairs and not bear weight etc., As per wound certificate he sustained grievous injury. On perusal of said cross examination it can be come to the conclusion that, the offending bus bearing reg.No.KA- 06-B-9051 does not holding valid permit as on the date of alleged accident. Therefore, lets rely on the citation reported in (2018) 8 Supreme Court Cases 492 (Rani and others Vs. National Insurance Company Limited and others) wherein it is held that: " Defence raised by insurer that offending vehicle did not possess a valid permit to operate in the State concerned - Accepting that defence, High Court absolving the insurer and fastening the liability on the insured i.e., the owner of offending vehicle directing him to satisfy the award - Held, even in such a case, the compensation determined must be first paid by the insurer, who could thereafter recover the same from the owner of offending vehicle - Order of High Court modified accordingly". Civil Appeal No.2253 of 2018 (Amrit Paul Singh and SCCH - 09 17 MVC No.269/2022 another Vs. Tata AIG General Ins. Co., Ltd., and others) wherein it is held that: "The insurer, the first respondent herein, opposed the claim on the ground that, the vehicle in question was driven in violation of the terms of the insurance policy and further the driver was not having a valid and effective driving license and, therefore, it was not obliged to indemnify the insured.
